items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The fellows in the orchestra, a lot of whom I knew personally, they were extremely nice. They made me feel so comfortable, guys like Johnny Ware...

ctx.x: What was that like, to finally realize that dream of playing with them?

That was great. That was great. That was wonderful. It really was nice. I’m positive that he did that because he felt that I deserved a crack at it. I wasn’t going to become a member or anything like that, but he just did it as a way of saying, “Look, this is what I think of you.” The fellows in the orchestra, a lot of whom I knew personally, they were extremely nice. They made me feel so comfortable, guys like Johnny Ware and Carmen [?Funarato] and people like that. They were so wonderful, and they’re first-rate…
When did that happen? Was that in the ’60s that you played with them?
